answer_points: Atoms with the same number of protons (atoms of the same element, or with the same atomic number, is also accepted).
worked_example.question:
Chadwick's experiments showed the existence of neutrons in an atom.

This led to an understanding of isotopes.

Define the term 'isotopes'.

Refer to subatomic particles in your answer.
worked_example.tip: The question asks for subatomic particles, so name protons and neutrons. References to electrons are ignored.

checks.q: An atom of fluorine has atomic number 9 and mass number 19. Give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons.
Give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in a Mg²⁺ ion (atomic number 12, mass number 24).

checks.a: Atoms of the same element, with the same number of protons, but with different numbers of neutrons.
checks.q: Describe what is meant by isotopes.

key_idea: The **atomic number** is the number of protons. The **mass number** is the number of protons plus neutrons. Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are **isotopes**.

blocks.text: Two numbers describe every atom. This section covers what they mean and how to use them to count particles.

items.meaning: The number of protons in an atom. It is the smaller number in the periodic table box.
The sum of the protons and neutrons in an atom. It is the larger number.

items: The mass number is written at the top left of the symbol. The atomic number is at the bottom left.
Aluminium is written ²⁷₁₃Al. Its mass number is 27 and its atomic number is 13.
Atoms of the same element always have the same atomic number. No two elements share an atomic number.

items.text: Aluminium has atomic number 13, so 13 protons.
An atom is neutral, so it has 13 electrons.

diagram.question: An atom has atomic number **{Z}** and mass number **{A}**. Calculate the number of neutrons in the atom.

items: Atomic number = number of protons. In an atom it is also the number of electrons.

blocks.text: An ion has an electric charge because its numbers of protons and electrons are not equal.

items.meaning: An atom (or group of atoms) that has lost or gained electrons, so it has an overall charge.

items: The atomic number and mass number do not change when an ion forms. Only the electrons change.
A positive ion has fewer electrons than protons.
A negative ion has more electrons than protons.

items.text: The atomic number gives the protons.
Protons minus the charge. For 3+ take away 3. For 2− add 2.

items: Only the number of electrons changes when an ion forms.
Electrons = protons − charge. A 2− ion has two more electrons than protons.

blocks.text: Atoms of one element can have different numbers of neutrons. These atoms are isotopes.

items.meaning: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

items: Isotopes have the same atomic number, because they are the same element.
Isotopes have different mass numbers, because the number of neutrons is different.
Chadwick's discovery of neutrons helped to explain isotopes.
Isotopes: same number of protons, different number of neutrons.
Different neutrons means a different mass number.
Always answer in terms of protons and neutrons.
